links.outcome: Readability of chatbot responses on pediatric fracture questions (Flesch-Kincaid, Flesch Reading Ease, Gunning Fog)
links.effect: Supplementary information had complex readability; Gemini more readable than ChatGPT-3.5 (Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level P=0.002, Flesch Reading Ease P<0.001, Gunning Fog P=0.021), but overall complexity was high.
links.quote: While AI chatbots provided responses with reasonable accuracy, most supplemental information required modification and had complex readability.

links.outcome: Chatbot accuracy and completeness versus AAOS clinical practice guideline recommendations
links.effect: Accurate in 11/13 (ChatGPT-4.0), 9/13 (ChatGPT-3.5), 11/13 (Gemini); incomplete in 3/13, 4/13, 4/13; no significant differences (accuracy P=0.533).
links.quote: ChatGPT-4.0, ChatGPT-3.5, and Google Gemini were accurate in 11/13, 9/13, and 11/13, supplementary in 13/13, 11/13, and 13/13, and incomplete in 3/13, 4/13, and 4/13 recommendations, respectively.

screen.reason: The study empirically benchmarks the accuracy and readability of ChatGPT-3.5, ChatGPT-4, and Google Gemini against AAOS clinical practice guidelines for pediatric fractures, without evaluating a specific implementation safeguard or deployment practice.
